reason: No candidate measurements or paired controls are supplied; the historical scores are noisy and do not establish causes. I rank localized changes to the fixed-size K loops first because they preserve the tile mapping and fallback. The pipelined schedule has a clear testable load/compute overlap hypothesis; address-generation changes are also bounded, though assembly_audit overlaps that idea and should be tested as its own proposal. The two-step variants overlap each other and the pipeline proposal, so separate their outcomes. Traversal, layout, and packing changes need broader pointer or memory-layout rewrites, which raise correctness risk and may add timed work. Tail handling targets only the fallback and offers little evidence of improving the fixed n=512 score.
